Renovation Wiring & Complete Home Rewiring in Melbourne's West

Energy Safe Victoria Licensed Electrical Contractors · REC 29064

Service Summary

Renovation wiring and home rewiring involves removing degraded, ungrounded, or non-compliant cabling and installing modern thermal-rated TPS circuits, sub-boards, power points, and architectural lighting. Bara Electrical Servicing ensures seamless integration for kitchen makeovers, home extensions, and full restorations across Melbourne's West.

Precision Electrical Integration for Renovations & Extensions

Renovating a home is the ideal time to modernize your electrical infrastructure before plaster and tiles are sealed. Whether updating an older brick home in Sunshine or extending a family residence in Caroline Springs, we coordinate directly with your builders and cabinetmakers.

Complete House Rewiring Services

  • Elimination of Hazardous Wiring: Removal of Vulcanised Indian Rubber (VIR), split-metal conduit, and ungrounded circuits.
  • High-Capacity Kitchen & Bath Circuits: Induction cooktop circuits, under-cabinet LED task lighting, pop-up island power points, and 3-in-1 bathroom heater/exhaust units.
  • Sub-Board Installations: Dedicated sub-switchboards for detached studios, outdoor entertainment pavilions, and garages.
  • Outdoor Entertaining & Alfresco Power: Weatherproof outdoor power points, infrared patio heaters, garden spotlighting, and pool pump connections.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know if my house needs rewiring?+

Homes built before 1980 often contain degraded black rubber (VIR) cabling, metal conduits, cotton-insulated conductors, or ungrounded lighting circuits that fail modern safety standards.

Can rewiring be done while we live in the house?+

Yes. We work room-by-room, restoring essential circuits and refrigeration at the end of each working day whenever possible.

Do kitchen renovations require dedicated electrical circuits?+

Yes. Modern kitchens require separate circuits for induction cooktops (often 32A), pyrolytic ovens, dishwashers, and microwave combination units to avoid circuit tripping.
